best_architecture: Orchestrator-worker (lead/sub-agent) fan-out/fan-in on top of a dependency DAG, executed with asyncio structured concurrency. Recommended layering for Local-Claw's Python asyncio orchestrator: (1) PLANNING LAYER - the lead agent (Gemma 4 MoE as orchestrator, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B as fallback/specialist worker) decomposes the task into a set of typed sub-tasks and emits a dependency DAG (edges = data/ordering dependencies), validated up front with Kahn's algorithm topological sort so deadlocks/cycles are caught at plan time rather than at runtime (the LLMCompiler / PlanCompiler pattern). (2) SCHEDULING LAYER - a deterministic, non-LLM scheduler walks the DAG in topological order and dispatches each node the moment all its dependencies have completed, so independent siblings run in parallel while dependent ones wait. Use asyncio.TaskGroup (Python 3.11+) rather than asyncio.gather for the per-wave fan-out: TaskGroup gives structured concurrency (no orphaned tasks, automatic sibling cancellation on first failure, typed ExceptionGroup via 'except*'), which is critical for clean failure recovery; keep gather(return_exceptions=True) only as a fallback for pre-3.11 or for very large best-effort batches where you do NOT want one failure to cancel siblings. (3) CONCURRENCY-CONTROL LAYER - dual gating: an asyncio.Semaphore bounds the number of in-flight sub-agents (protects local GPU/VRAM for Gemma/Qwen and any remote API), plus a token-aware rate limiter enforcing BOTH RPM and TPM with a sliding-window / token-bucket and an ~80% safety margin; pre-estimate prompt tokens with the model tokenizer before admitting a task so TPM is respected proactively. Track a global token budget shared across all parallel agents (atomic counter guarded by an asyncio.Lock) and refuse/queue new spawns once the budget ceiling is hit - roughly 80% of multi-agent quality variance is explained by token spend, so the budget is the primary tuning knob. (4) AGGREGATION LAYER - fan-in via a reducer. For deterministic merges (e.g., code files, tool results) collect TaskGroup results directly; for QUALITY aggregation of overlapping/competing LLM outputs use a Mixture-of-Agents (MoA) aggregator: a layered scheme where proposer agents generate candidate answers in parallel and an aggregator agent synthesizes them into a single higher-quality response (optionally multiple MoA layers). (5) INTER-AGENT COMMUNICATION - prefer message-passing/state-handoff over shared mutable state: each sub-agent gets its own context window and returns a condensed result to the orchestrator (Anthropic's 'subagents as intelligent filters' pattern). Externalize the orchestrator's plan/state to memory (MongoDB/Redis here) BEFORE the context fills rather than relying on a larger window. Key design decisions that matter most: structured concurrency over fire-and-forget; dual RPM+TPM limiting with a shared token budget; DAG topo-sort validated at plan time; orchestrator on the stronger model and workers on cheaper/faster models; condensed result hand-back to avoid context bloat; and adaptive sub-agent count (1 for simple lookups, 2-4 for comparisons, 10+ for complex decomposition) to avoid over-spawning. [uncertain] The exact optimal sub-agent fan-out count and token-budget ceiling for the local Gemma/Qwen models should be tuned empirically, since published guidance (3-5 subagents, 15x token cost) comes from Anthropic's cloud Opus/Sonnet setup, not local 4-bit MoE models.
reference_papers: Mixture-of-Agents Enhances Large Language Model Capabilities (Wang et al. 2024) - arxiv:2406.04692 - layered MoA: parallel proposer agents per layer + aggregator synthesizing previous-layer outputs; 65.1% AlpacaEval 2.0 with open-source models, surpassing GPT-4 Omni. Core reference for quality-oriented fan-in aggregation.

An LLM Compiler for Parallel Function Calling (Kim et al. 2024, ICML 2024) - arxiv:2312.04511 - planner emits a DAG of tool/function calls with explicit dependency edges; executor topologically schedules and dispatches nodes as soon as dependencies finish, enabling parallel execution that reduces latency and token cost vs sequential ReAct. Core reference for DAG-based parallel scheduling.

Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling (Brown et al. 2024) - arxiv:2407.21787 - establishes that parallel repeated sampling (fan-out) plus a verifier/selector improves coverage and final quality; relevant to spawning N parallel attempts and aggregating the best.

AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation (Wu et al. 2023) - arxiv:2308.08155 - conversational multi-agent framework; foundational reference for message-passing inter-agent communication and group-chat coordination patterns.

Multi-Agent Design: Optimizing Agents with Better Prompts and Topologies (2025) - arxiv:2502.02533 - studies how agent topology (including parallel/fan-out structures) and prompts affect multi-agent system quality; useful for choosing aggregation topology. [uncertain] exact author list and final venue not verified.
reference_repos: togethercomputer/MoA - reference implementation of Mixture-of-Agents (layered proposer + aggregator) achieving 65.1% on AlpacaEval; canonical pattern for quality fan-in aggregation - https://github.com/togethercomputer/moa

langchain-ai/langgraph - graph-based orchestration with the Send() API for runtime map-reduce fan-out/fan-in, built on asyncio; typed state, checkpointers (memory/SQLite/Postgres), parallel superstep execution - https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph

crewAIInc/crewAI - role-based multi-agent framework with Crews (dynamic role delegation) + Flows (deterministic event-driven orchestration); good for parallel role-delegated task execution - https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI

microsoft/autogen - multi-agent conversation framework (GroupChat, message-passing); now in maintenance mode in favor of Microsoft Agent Framework but still a key reference for inter-agent communication patterns - https://github.com/microsoft/autogen

SqueezeAILab/LLMCompiler - official LLMCompiler implementation: planner builds a DAG of function calls, executor runs them in parallel with topological scheduling - https://github.com/SqueezeAILab/LLMCompiler

anthropics/claude-cookbook (formerly anthropic-cookbook) - includes orchestrator-worker / parallel sub-agent examples and the multi-agent research-system patterns described in Anthropic's engineering blog - https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-cookbook
key_libraries: asyncio (Python stdlib, Python 3.11+) - use asyncio.TaskGroup for structured concurrency (no orphans, sibling cancellation, ExceptionGroup via except*) as the primary fan-out primitive; asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True) as best-effort fallback; asyncio.Semaphore for concurrency capping; asyncio.Lock for the shared token-budget counter.

aiolimiter (Python, ~1.1.x) - asyncio-native leaky-bucket rate limiter (AsyncLimiter) for enforcing requests-per-minute; compose two limiters (or a custom token-aware limiter) to gate both RPM and TPM.
tenacity (Python, ~8.x/9.x) - retry with exponential backoff + jitter (retry, stop_after_attempt, wait_random_exponential) for handling 429s / transient sub-agent failures within each task.

tiktoken (Python, ~0.7+/0.8+) - fast tokenizer for pre-estimating prompt/completion tokens to enforce TPM and the global token budget before admitting a task. [uncertain] for local Gemma/Qwen models the matching HF tokenizer (transformers AutoTokenizer) should be used instead of tiktoken's OpenAI BPE for accurate counts.

langgraph (Python, 0.x heading to v1.0 ~Oct 2025) - graph orchestration with Send() API for dynamic runtime map-reduce fan-out/fan-in, typed state + reducers, checkpointing; strong fit for the DAG/parallel orchestration layer.
crewai (Python, 0.x) - higher-level role-based crews + deterministic Flows for parallel role-delegated agents; faster to prototype than LangGraph.

graphlib (Python stdlib, 3.9+) - graphlib.TopologicalSorter provides built-in topological sort with get_ready()/done() for incremental DAG scheduling, ideal for a dependency-aware async scheduler without external deps.

anyio (Python, 4.x) - optional structured-concurrency abstraction (task groups, capacity limiters) that works across asyncio/trio; useful if backend portability or pre-3.11 TaskGroup semantics are needed.
networkx (Python, 3.x) - optional, for building/validating/visualizing the dependency DAG (cycle detection, topological_sort) when the graph is complex; graphlib suffices for lightweight needs.
